mainTopic: Cancelling future vows on ראש השנה, keeping it out of public lectures, and whether the רבנן disagree with רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
overview: The גמרא first fills in missing words in the משנה, splitting it into two rules. Pressing a friend with a vow to eat with you is just a נדרי זירוזין, a vow of urging. Separately, anyone who wants his vows for the year to have no force can declare on ראש השנה that all his future vows are cancelled. The גמרא asks how the משנה's condition, 'as long as he remembers at the time of the vow,' can work: if he remembers and vows anyway, he has dropped his condition. אביי answers by changing the wording to 'as long as he does NOT remember.' רבא keeps the wording and explains that he remembers there was a condition but not what it covered, so the vow is cancelled only if he says he is vowing based on his earlier intention. רבא then scolds רב הונא בר חיננא for planning to teach this method in a public lecture, since the תנא hid it so people would not treat vows lightly. Finally, the גמרא asks whether the רבנן disagree with רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, and if so, whether the הלכה follows him. It begins a proof from a later משנה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה is missing words: two separate rules
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers its difficulty with the משנה by saying words are missing. It then fills them in as two separate rules: a vow of urging, and the ראש השנה declaration that cancels future vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some words are missing from the משנה, and it really teaches this: If someone wants his friend to eat with him, keeps pressing him, and makes a vow about it, that is just a vow of urging. Separately, someone who wants none of his vows to stand for the whole year should get up on ראש השנה and say: 'Every vow I will make in the future should be cancelled.' This works as long as he remembers at the time of the vow.
steps.whatsHappening: Just before this, the גמרא had a problem with how the משנה was worded. Now it answers by filling in missing words, which splits the משנה into two separate teachings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case of pressing a friend to eat is simply a נדרי זירוזין, which needs no cancelling at all. The ראש השנה declaration is a separate, general method for anyone who wants his future vows to have no force. The added line 'as long as he remembers at the time of the vow' is what the next step will question.

keyTerms.meaning: Something is missing from the text; the גמרא fills in the missing words
Vows of urging: vows said only to pressure someone, which are not taken as real binding vows
Presses him / keeps urging him
Makes a vow concerning him
Remembers (the ראש השנה declaration) at the moment of making the vow

steps.confusionAlert: There are now TWO separate rules. The vow of urging needs no ראש השנה declaration at all. The declaration is a different tool for someone who wants all his vows for the year to have no force.

phrases.english: The משנה is missing words, and this is what it teaches:
One who wants his friend to eat with him
and presses him and makes a vow about him,
this is a vow of urging.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָרוֹצֶה שֶׁלֹּא יִתְקַיְּימוּ נְדָרָיו כׇּל הַשָּׁנָה,
phrases.english: And one who wants his vows not to stand the whole year
should stand up on ראש השנה and say:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל נֶדֶר שֶׁאֲנִי עָתִיד לִידּוֹר יְהֵא בָּטֵל,
phrases.english: 'Every vow that I will make in the future should be cancelled,'
as long as he remembers at the time of the vow.
phrases.notes: He means remembering the ראש השנה declaration at the moment he makes the new vow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a difficulty raised just before this section by restoring missing words to the משנה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual completion: missing words are filled in
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to tie the ראש השנה declaration to the case of pressing a friend to eat
steps.terutzMaskana: Two separate rules: pressing a friend is a vow of urging, and the ראש השנה declaration is a general method for cancelling future vows

steps.title: If he remembers, he has dropped his condition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the line 'as long as he remembers.' If he remembers his declaration and still makes the vow, he has given up the condition and confirmed the vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he remembers, then he has uprooted his condition and confirmed his vow!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last line of the restored משנה. Remembering the declaration should make it fail, not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who knows he cancelled all future vows and goes ahead and vows anyway is clearly showing he wants this vow to count. So remembering should undo the ראש השנה condition, which is the opposite of what the משנה says.

keyTerms.meaning: He uprooted his condition (cancelled his own earlier stipulation)
He confirmed his vow (made it binding)

phrases.english: If he remembers, he has uprooted his condition,
and confirmed his vow!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the final clause of the restored משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The clause 'וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיְּהֵא זָכוּר בִּשְׁעַת הַנֶּדֶר'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Knowingly vowing despite the declaration shows he wants the vow to count, so the condition should be cancelled, not upheld

steps.title: אביי corrects the wording: 'as long as he does NOT remember'
steps.stepSummary: אביי fixes the wording of the משנה. The declaration works only if he does not remember it when he vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Teach it this way: 'as long as he does not remember at the time of the vow.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by changing the wording. The declaration cancels the vow only when the person has forgotten about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he forgot the declaration, his new vow does not show any decision to drop the condition, so the condition still cancels it. If he remembered and vowed anyway, the condition is gone. This turns the משנה's line into its opposite.

keyTerms.meaning: That he will not remember

phrases.english: אביי said: Teach it this way:
phrases.notes: אביי is changing the wording of the משנה, adding the word 'not.'

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא זָכוּר בִּשְׁעַת הַנֶּדֶר.
phrases.english: 'as long as he does not remember at the time of the vow.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by correcting the text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה requires that he remember the declaration
steps.terutzMaskana: The declaration works only if he does not remember it at the time of the vow

steps.title: רבא keeps the wording: he only half-remembers
steps.stepSummary: רבא keeps the original wording, 'as long as he remembers.' He explains it as a case where the person knows he made a condition but is unsure what it covered, so it depends on what he says when he vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Really, it is as we said at first. What case are we dealing with? He made a condition on ראש השנה but does not know which vows it covered, and now he makes a vow. If he remembers at the time of the vow and says, 'I am vowing based on my earlier intention,' his vow has no substance. If he did not say, 'I am vowing based on my earlier intention,' he has uprooted his condition and confirmed his vow.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer to the challenge without changing any words in the משנה. He explains the case so that 'remembering' fits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'remembering' means he recalls that he made some condition but is not sure what it covered. If, at the moment of vowing, he says he is relying on that earlier intention, the vow is empty. If he says nothing, the plain new vow wins and the condition is dropped.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, it is as we said at first (keep the original version)
What case are we dealing with here? (opens a specific explanation of the case)
Based on the first (earlier) intention
It has no substance; it means nothing

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers. אביי changes the text: the declaration works only if he forgot it. רבא keeps the text: he remembers there was a condition, and the vow is cancelled only if he says 'I am vowing based on my earlier intention.'

phrases.english: רבא said:
Really, it is as we said at first.
phrases.notes: He means the original version, 'as long as he remembers,' without אביי's change.

phrases.english: What case are we dealing with here?
Where he made a condition on ראש השנה
but does not know which vows his condition covered.
And now he makes a vow.
If he remembers at the time of the vow
and says, 'I am vowing based on my earlier intention,'
his vow has no substance.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אָמַר ״עַל דַּעַת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה אֲנִי נוֹדֵר״ —
phrases.english: If he did not say, 'I am vowing based on my earlier intention,'
he has uprooted his condition and confirmed his vow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the same challenge, without אביי's change to the text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Remembering the declaration means he knowingly gave it up
steps.terutzMaskana: He remembers there was a condition but not its details; the vow is cancelled only if he says he is vowing based on his earlier intention

steps.title: רבא objects to teaching this method in public
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חיננא wanted to teach the ראש השנה method in a public lecture. רבא objected: the תנא hid it on purpose so people would not treat vows lightly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר חיננא planned to teach this in the public lecture. רבא said to him: The תנא deliberately hid it so that people would not treat vows lightly, and you want to teach it in the public lecture?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story about whether this method should be taught to everyone. רבא says no.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why the משנה's wording was unclear in the first place: the תנא left the method hidden on purpose. If everyone knew they could cancel all their vows in advance, they might make vows carelessly. So the הלכה is real, but it is not to be spread in public.

keyTerms.meaning: A public lecture (given to the general community, such as on a festival)
To teach it publicly / expound it
Deliberately conceals it; leaves it vague
Lightheadedness; treating something lightly

steps.whyThisMatters: It explains why the משנה needed the 'missing words' at the start: the תנא left the method vague on purpose. It also teaches that a הלכה may be true and still not taught in public, to protect people from taking vows lightly.
steps.whatToRemember: The ראש השנה cancelling of vows is valid, but רבא held it should not be publicized, so people would not treat vows lightly.

phrases.english: רב הונא בר חיננא planned
to teach it in the public lecture.
רבא said to him:
The תנא deliberately hides it

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִנְהֲגוּ קַלּוּת רֹאשׁ בִּנְדָרִים,
phrases.english: so that people should not treat vows lightly,
and you want to teach it in the public lecture?!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִינָּנָא סָבַר לְמִידְרְשֵׁיהּ בְּפִירְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining how the ראש השנה method works, the גמרא tells a story about whether it should be taught publicly
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The method of cancelling vows on ראש השנה should not be taught in public, so people will not treat vows lightly

steps.title: A two-part question about רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the רבנן disagree with רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's ruling in the משנה. It then asks: if they do disagree, is the הלכה like him?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: Do the רבנן disagree with רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, or not? And if you decide that they do disagree, is the הלכה like him, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the משנה. It asks whether רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's ruling is a disputed opinion, and if it is, whether we follow it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה brings this rule only in the name of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, so it is unclear whether the other רבנן hold differently. The question is built in two layers. First, is there an argument at all? Only if there is an argument do we need to ask whose side the הלכה follows.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised among the scholars. It is an honest open question, not an attack.
They disagree.
And if you come to say. It introduces a follow-up question that only applies if the first answer goes a certain way.
The הלכה follows his view.

steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate questions here, not one. The second question, about whose view is the הלכה, only comes up if the answer to the first is 'yes, they disagree.'

phrases.english: A question was asked among them:

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב,
phrases.english: Do the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov,
or not?
And if you say that they disagree,
is the halakha in accordance with him, or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב, אוֹ לָא?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא's comment about not teaching the ראש השנה method in public, the גמרא goes back to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's rule in the משנה and asks about its status.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the רבנן disagree with רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, and if they do, whether the הלכה follows him.

steps.title: Starting a proof from a later משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to answer the question by quoting another משנה, which opens with 'One who says to his friend…'. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear a proof, as we learned in a משנה: One who says to his friend…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a proof. It starts quoting a משנה from later in the מסכת to help answer the question, but the case itself is only spelled out on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'תא שמע' tells us a source is coming that may settle the question. So far we only have the opening words, 'one who says to his friend.' We have to wait for the rest of the case to see how it connects to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

keyTerms.meaning: One who says to his friend. This is the opening of the case being quoted.

phrases.english: Come and hear, as we learned in a mishna:
One who says to his friend:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It begins answering the two-part question from Step 6 by bringing a משנה as evidence.
steps.raayaObject: The question of whether the רבנן disagree with רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, and whether the הלכה follows him.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה later in the מסכת that begins 'One who says to his friend'. Its content continues on the next amud.
